t: Woodford County becomes the first Kentucky county to ban data centers permanently
b: The unanimous vote was tied to farmland preservation and local opposition, with the judge-executive pointing to a fight in neighboring Mercer County as a warning.

t: TVA creates a data center rate class with higher rates and upfront commitments
b: Approved at a Memphis board meeting, it raises data center rates about 10% on average over three years and requires capacity commitments to fund transmission and connections, so households don't foot the bill.

t: Louisville adopts a six-month pause on new data center applications
b: The pause covers specified rezoning, conditional-use and development-plan applications while the city writes rules, amid opposition to a planned hyperscale facility in West Louisville.

t: Knoxville pauses large data centers for a year
b: The emergency ordinance halts permits and construction for data centers needing 10 MW or more while planners write zoning rules, since the city code doesn't define the use.

t: Knox County adopts a one-year data center moratorium, 10–0
b: The pause runs through June 30, 2027, or until the county adopts data center rules. Knoxville followed with its own pause in July.

t: Anderson, Morgan and Loudon counties pause data centers; Blount sets strict rules
b: Anderson and Morgan adopted two-year pauses and Loudon a six-month one. Blount limits data centers to industrial zones, 5,000 feet from homes, schools and churches, with a 60-decibel cap.

t: Mason County rezones about 2,080 acres for a proposed data center campus
b: The vote moved 28 properties north of Germantown Road to rural industrial zoning after the county adopted rules for data centers in unincorporated areas.
iw: Land cleared for a large campus

w: NAACP, Young, Gifted & Green and Safe and Sound Coalition
t: Groups appeal Mississippi's permit for 41 xAI turbines in Southaven
b: SELC filed the appeal of the March 10 permit, which does not cover the temporary turbines already running at the site.

t: Alabama cuts new data center tax breaks to 20 years
b: HB 399 caps abatements granted from 2027 at 20 years unless operators sign community investment deals, and makes 100 MW-plus sites pay state sales and non-school property taxes once open.

t: Bessemer rezones 914 more acres, expanding Project Marvel to about 1,600
b: QTS, owned by Blackstone funds, later confirmed it is behind the 18-building, 1,200 MW campus. The extra land is for wider buffers and layout flexibility.

t: Clarksdale conditionally rezones 648 acres for a possible hyperscale campus
b: No developer agreement or project approval had been announced by mid-July.

t: Bill to end a Mississippi data center income tax break dies
b: HB 4045 would have ended the income tax exemption for certain data center projects after 2026 and created a development fund tied to large fee-in-lieu deals. It died on the House calendar.

t: Hundreds pack a Southaven hearing; every speaker opposes xAI's turbine permit
b: Residents described health problems and constant noise they blame on the plant during the hearing on 41 permanent turbines, which regulators approved weeks later.

t: Meade County adopts a 12-month data center moratorium
b: The ordinance followed the county's October rejection of a 138-acre data center rezoning and directs planners to study impacts.

t: Sweetwater limits data centers to heavy industrial zones with a 60-decibel cap
b: The ordinance also requires five-acre lots and setbacks of 150 to 200 feet, rising to 500 feet next to homes.

t: Two Alabama utility commissioners lose GOP primaries amid anger over power bills
b: Jeremy Oden and Chip Beeker lost after widespread outcry over high electric bills, as data centers became a top election issue. Only Cynthia Almond will keep her seat next year.

t: Memphis pollution board dismisses the appeal of xAI's turbine permit, 6–1
b: SELC's July appeal argued the permit ignored xAI's unpermitted turbines and misread the Clean Air Act. The board found the case moot because most turbines had been removed.

t: Alabama freezes power rates through 2027 and approves solar for a Meta data center
b: The 3–0 vote delayed the Lindsay Hill gas plant charge to 2028 and approved two Baldwin County solar farms serving Meta. Critics said the freeze postpones costs rather than avoiding them.
iw: Rates frozen, data center supply added

t: Residents rally against Project Marvel days before Bessemer's rezoning vote
b: Speakers at the Legacy YMCA cited noise, diesel generator pollution, heavy water use and a rare fish, the Birmingham darter, and said officials hadn't answered their questions.

t: Kentucky regulators let LG&E/KU build $3 billion in gas plants for data centers
b: The PSC approved two new units for an expected 1,470 MW of load growth but rejected a special cost-recovery mechanism and barred construction if the forecast demand doesn't materialize.

t: Memphis steers 25% of xAI's property taxes to nearby neighborhoods
b: The ordinance covers both Colossus sites and a planned water recycling plant, capped at $100 million for projects within five miles. A bid to raise the share to 75% failed.

t: Advocates rally at Kentucky PSC as LG&E/KU seeks gas plants for data centers
b: Outside the hearing, critics said the proposed tariff for 100 MW-plus users, which requires paying for 80% of contracted energy for 15 years, only protects customers if the data centers get built.

t: Mississippi lets xAI run temporary gas turbines in Southaven without permits
b: After an xAI affiliate bought a former Duke Energy plant in July, regulators treated its turbines for Colossus 2 as exempt temporary units. The count reached 27 by December, and neighbors complained of noise.

t: Regulators let Alabama Power buy a $622 million gas plant for data center demand
b: The Lindsay Hill plant in Autauga County was bought to meet growth driven largely by data centers. A later rate freeze pushed the roughly $3.32 monthly customer charge for it to 2028.

t: Shelby County permits 15 gas turbines at xAI's Memphis data center
b: xAI had installed as many as 35 turbines without permits over the prior year. The department also ruled that temporary turbines need no permit, a stance critics said opened a loophole.

t: Residents' lawsuit briefly halts Bessemer's Project Marvel rezoning
b: A judge's April order blocked a council vote over inadequate public notice, and the city restarted the process. The council approved the rezoning in November, and the suit was later dismissed.

t: Bessemer officials sign a secrecy agreement with Project Marvel's developer
b: The mayor, city attorney and chief of staff agreed not to share developer names, site plans or studies. The city released the agreement in July 2026 after environmental groups threatened to sue.

t: Mississippi offers tax breaks for Compass's $10 billion Meridian campus
b: State certification brings 10-year income and franchise tax exemptions and sales tax breaks on construction materials and equipment, plus a $4 million legislative site grant. Mississippi Power will supply about 500 MW.
iw: State incentives for a hyperscale campus
